title: Privilege Mesh & Zone Anchoring — compact RBAC v2 surface
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define a compact, expressive role model for RBAC v2 that maps cleanly to Redwood's multi-tenant resource topology and simplifies auditability and SSO/SAML onboarding. This ticket captures the 'privilege mesh' abstraction (roles + capability edges) and a complementary 'resource zone' anchoring model that bounds permissions to logical resource zones (org, workspace, runtime-pool, region). The design must: (1) make permission resolution efficient (O(depth) preferrable), (2) support deterministic explainability for audit logs and the Console 'why-can-I' explainer, (3) enable straightforward mappings from SAML groups and external identity attributes, (4) provide safe admin controls (breakglass, escalation policies, expiration), and (5) define a migration path from v1 roles and the current roleset catalog.

Key components proposed: privilege mesh (compact set of canonical capabilities rather than per-action permissions), zone anchors (explicit binding of a role to a resource zone with optional exclusion lists), lateral capability edges (a small graph allowing scoped privilege delegation for service-accounts and automation), evaluation order rules (zone-specific first, then principal-specific, then global fallbacks), cache invalidation hooks for role/zone updates, and audit enrichment schema for explainability (role_id, anchor_zone, effective_permissions, policy_trace).
decisions: Adopt capability-oriented privileges (read, write, manage, deploy, observe, admin) rather than thousands of granular action constants
Introduce 'resource zones' as core scoping primitives: Organization, Workspace, Pool, Region, Project — roles are anchored to one or more zones
Evaluation order will prioritize most-specific anchors (exact resource) -> zone -> tenant-global, with deterministic tie-breaker by role precedence value
Audit logs will include policy_trace: ordered list of matched bindings with reasons and TTLs for any temporary elevations
Keep role objects compact: name, capabilities[], anchors[], precedence:int, metadata -> reduces cache size and speeds lookup
open_questions: How to express deny semantics in the compact mesh without introducing full policy language? (explicit deny flags vs. deny-roles)
Should we support composable derived roles (role templates that expand into multiple capability anchors) or keep expansion server-side only?
What is the precise mapping contract between SAML groups/claims and internal anchors (group -> role vs group -> anchor+role binding)?
How to represent cross-zone delegation safely (e.g., CI runner in Pool A needs deploy rights in Pool B for a limited window)?
